cases.note: When the gameplay pause menu opens, temporarily hide the FPS and graphics-preset lines even if F3 enabled them. Keep the date and time visible at the same top-right position. After resume restore the prior F3 preference, including when that preference was off. Check narrow and wide window bounds and switching an F4 preset after resume. Preserve the live interaction hint without an empty objective row and keep waypoint distance updating.
acceptance: Pause hides FPS and preset lines while the clock stays visible and fixed.
Resume restores both prior F3 states and F4 still works after resume.
Verify narrow and wide bounds, interaction hints and waypoint distance.

cases.note: When a solo trip loads a campaign from its last good backup because the primary save is corrupt or absent, show a brief one-time in-game recovery notice on entering that trip. A healthy primary or a fresh slot must not show it. Preserve the recovered backup on the next successful save, resume normal rotation on a later save and leave the catch journal untouched. Do not add saved fields or change crew behavior. Run the existing save recovery checks against isolated fixture data.
acceptance: A corrupt or missing primary with a valid backup gives exactly one solo recovery notice.
A healthy primary, fresh slot and crew sessions give no recovery notice.
First and later saves retain existing rotation behavior and journal schema. The recovery test passes.

cases.note: Give a road-car guest driver a brief HUD status while the host is braking because that guest's driving input expired. Clear the status when the host receives fresh input and when the guest leaves the seat. Check simulated missing input during a turn and recovery by the same driver. Use host-authoritative status, keep steering, braking, camera and engine mix unchanged and do not show the status to other riders or solo players.
acceptance: The host detects expiry and only the assigned guest sees the status.
Fresh input and seat exit clear the status, including a later re-entry.
Host braking, pose application, seats, camera and engine mix retain their behavior.
Verify input loss and recovery in an isolated host/guest setup or report what remains untested.
